$description: Catalog-vs-disk audit. Compares each entry in the frozen instrument catalog snapshot against an observed sample-library disk index, classifying matched / missing / ambiguous rows + duplicate-claim and unmatched-file diagnostics. `contentHash` is a SHA-256 over the canonical bytes of summary + matched + missing + ambiguous + duplicateCandidates + unmatchedDiskFiles; auditedAt and sampleRoot are outside the hashed region so the audit identity depends only on (catalog state, disk state).

LEGACY_PROVENANCE.rules: Each catalog row is resolved against an ordered list of candidate relative paths produced by named join rules. The first rule whose path exists on disk wins; if none match, the row is reported missing with every candidate listed. Rules in order: [simple] {family} - {lowLevel} - {mainStyle} - [{library} - ]{preset}[ - {key}].mp3 — nulls skipped; key appended only when present.  |  [fx-key-bpm] fx rows where the catalog preset ends with " - {bpm}": strip that suffix and format the file as "{prefix} - {presetStem} - {key} {bpm}bpm.mp3".  |  [simple-enharmonic] Simple rule with enharmonic-sharp key spelling (catalog flat → disk sharp: Eb→D#, Bb→A#, Db→C#, Gb→F#, Ab→G#). Only emits a candidate when the catalog key is flat-spelled.  |  [fx-key-bpm-enharmonic] fx-key-bpm rule with enharmonic-sharp key spelling. Only fires when the catalog key is flat-spelled.

aliasesApplied.reason: docs/58e — build-snapshot.ts post-import reclassification rewrites fxOther+mainStyle=8bit rows to fx8bitArcade so per-lowLevelType volume tuning can target the 15 retro-arcade samples independently of generic fxOther. Disk keeps them under fxOther (where the user/Stefan filed them). Catalog name is authoritative until the disk is reorganised. Verified that fx/fxOther/ contains ONLY arcade content (15 files, all DonkeyKong/Frogger/MsPacMan/PacMan/nintendo).
